title: Reversing Lamp Switch Removal and Refitting
introduction:
I find the electrical connector in the wider drawing first, then use the close-up to identify the reversing lamp switch on the transmission. Freeing the connector and its harness guide before removing the switch keeps the lead from becoming a telephone cord wound around the fitting.

This procedure covers the illustrated switch’s removal and refitting, including hoist preparation. I finish with a secured, engine-off lamp check so the job ends with an observable result. That completion check is not a diagnosis of the reversing-lamp circuit.

items.name: Disable remote start
items.detail: Before working underneath or around the vehicle, disable remote start, if equipped, through the Central Display: Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup. Otherwise, the vehicle could be remotely started during service, causing personal injury or death.

items.name: Remove the key
items.detail: Switch the ignition OFF and remove the key from the vehicle to prevent another person from starting the engine during service. An accidental start can cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Eyes, ears and hands
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection during vehicle service, and protective gloves when handling pointed or sharp-edged parts. Failure to use this protection may result in serious personal injury.

items.name: Capacity and lift-arm placement
items.detail: Use a hoist with adequate capacity for the vehicle’s weight, including cargo and modifications. Position its lift arms at the locations shown in [Jacking and Lifting - Overview](#/document/G1663631). Identify the correct points by the triangles stamped into the unibody sheet metal or frame; the overview drawing shows their locations. Lifting elsewhere can make the vehicle shift or fall, causing serious personal injury. Incorrect hoist-arm placement can cause unintended movement, serious personal injury or death.

items.name: Adapter and fork clearance
items.detail: Before lifting, position the hoist adapters clear of suspension, exhaust and steering-linkage components to avoid damage. On a two-column hoist, keep the forks clear of suspension components, mounting brackets and stabilizer mounting brackets, if equipped. Position the hoist to avoid damaging the axle or rear cover.

items.name: Drive-on lift clearance
items.detail: If using a drive-on lift, check for interference before driving onto it. Contact with the lift can damage the underbody.

items.name: Drive-wheel restriction
items.detail: Do not use the engine to power the drive wheels unless all drive wheels are elevated clear of the ground. Ground contact can cause unintended vehicle movement, serious personal injury or death.

items.name: The vehicle jack is not service access
items.detail: The supplied vehicle jack is only for an emergency change of a deflated tire. Using it to raise the vehicle for other work can damage the vehicle. Never apply jack pressure to either bumper; this damages the bumper covers. The switch procedure calls for a hoist.

items.name: If a jack is used during preparation
items.detail: Check that its capacity covers the vehicle’s weight, cargo and modifications. Use the designated lifting points on a hard, level surface, set the parking brake and block every wheel remaining on the ground. After jacking, support the vehicle with jack stands or floor stands. Never get underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack: it can lower unexpectedly. Failure to observe these precautions can cause unintended vehicle movement, serious personal injury or death.

items.name: Controlled tightening
items.detail: Have a torque wrench suitable for the switch’s refitting torque, retained in the switch-removal block below. No tool size, sealant or replacement-fastener requirement is specified for this operation.

items.name: Keep the vehicle stationary
items.detail: Start on a hard, level surface with the parking brake applied and wheels on the ground chocked. Keep the parking brake applied during this repair. Establish secure support on the hoist before going underneath. Before lowering, clear tools and people from the lowering area; keep the parking brake applied and restore wheel chocks as the wheels reach the ground before releasing the vehicle from the hoist.

edits.text:
Raise the vehicle on a hoist using the designated lifting points.
Refer to: Jacking and Lifting - Overview (100-02 Jacking and Lifting, Description and Operation).
edits.why: The lifting overview identifies the support locations by stamped triangles and shows them in the underbody drawing. I establish that support and the required clearances before reaching the switch; the nearby transmission casing is not an invitation to improvise a lifting point.

edits.text: Disconnect the reversing lamp switch electrical connector, then release the connector from the wiring harness guide.
edits.why: In the wider illustration, the arrow identifies the connector connection and the highlighted lead runs toward the switch. The electrical connection and the guide attachment are separate things to release. Freeing both lets the switch lead come away with the switch instead of remaining tethered to the vehicle wiring.

edits.text:
Remove the reversing lamp switch identified in the close-up.
Refitting torque: 20 lb.ft (27 Nm)
edits.why: The close-up highlights the switch and its attached lead, distinguishing them from the neighboring connectors and tubing. The torque belongs to tightening the switch during installation; it is not a target for forcing the switch loose.

edits.text: Reverse the removal sequence: install the reversing lamp switch and tighten it to the refitting torque given above, secure its electrical connector in the wiring harness guide, and reconnect the connector. Lower the vehicle after the underbody work is complete.
edits.why:
Refitting restores both the electrical connection and the guide that controls the lead’s position. I use the wider drawing to check that the connector is back in its guide and the lead follows the illustrated route before finishing.

Once the vehicle is fully on the ground, keep the parking brake applied and wheels chocked. A driver stays at the controls holding the service brake; an observer stands safely to one side, outside the travel path. Keep the engine off and switch the ignition on. Select reverse and confirm the reversing lamps illuminate, then select Neutral and confirm they go out. Turn the ignition off, remove the key and restore the normal parked gear, retaining the parking brake and chocks until ready to move. This ordinary completion check follows the lamp response described in the [exterior lighting overview](#/document/G1694241). If the response is wrong, resolve the fault before relying on the lamps; this result alone does not identify the failed component.
